Play it at the feet with follow; stop it when they land. For a selection ring under a unit use state.selected; for a blazing power aura use state.aura.

effects.name: state.lucky
effects.whenToUse: The player has a luck buff or good-fortune bonus: a four-leaf clover or lucky charm picked up, a better drop or crit chance, a lucky streak in a slot or gacha game, a fortune blessing, a lucky cat bonus. Follow the character; stop it when the luck runs out. For a one-off stat boost use magic.buff; for invincibility use state.rainbow.

effects.name: state.marked
effects.whenToUse: A character or enemy is marked as a target: a hunter's mark, a lock-on before a missile hits, a bounty or "defeat this one" marker, an enemy that will take extra damage, the next target of a boss. Play it over the head with follow; stop it when the mark ends. For the moment the mark is placed use magic.mark; for a selection ring at a unit's feet use state.selected.

effects.name: state.overheat
effects.whenToUse: A character is overheated or far too hot: a desert or lava level, a heatwave, a sauna, a fever, eating something too spicy, a runner worn out in the sun. Follow the body; stop it when they cool down. For actually being on fire use state.burning; for a quick nervous sweat use state.sweat.

effects.name: state.possessed
effects.whenToUse: A character is possessed, corrupted or taken over by evil: a demon inside, a dark-magic berserk, a cursed hero turning villain, a boss's dark phase, mind control by a dark power. Follow the body; stop it when the evil leaves. For a bright power-up aura use state.aura; for a lingering curse or hex use state.cursed; for ghosts circling someone use state.haunted.

effects.name: state.purr
effects.whenToUse: A pet is calm and content: a cat purring on a lap, a dog being stroked, a hamster cuddled, a pet resting happily after care in a pet or virtual-pet game. Follow the head; stop it when the petting ends. For a lovestruck or charmed character use state.love; for a quick happy pop use state.happy.

effects.name: state.rally
effects.whenToUse: Soldiers or units are rallied, inspired or led: a morale or leadership bonus, troops near a hero, banner or commander, an army under a war-cry buff in strategy, RTS, tactics and medieval games. Play it at each unit's feet with follow and stop it when the bonus ends. For the shout itself use magic.warcry; for a move-order marker on the ground use world.rally; for a blazing power-up use state.aura.

effects.name: state.sick
effects.whenToUse: A character feels sick, nauseous or queasy: ate bad food, has a cold or flu, about to throw up after a ride, a car-sick pet, a fever in a care game. Follow the body; stop it when they feel better. For a poison damage status use state.poison; for tipsy or confused use state.drunk.

effects.name: state.sleepy
effects.whenToUse: A pet or cute character is drowsy, dozing or napping in a cosy, dreamy way: a sleepy kitten in its bed, bedtime in a kids or pet-care game, a pet whose energy is low and needs rest, a yawning baby animal. Follow the head; stop it when it wakes. For a plain asleep, idle or knocked-out status use state.sleep.

effects.name: state.slowed
effects.whenToUse: A character is slowed down for a while: a slow spell, sticky tar or glue, deep mud or snow, a snare, a heavy-weight debuff. Follow the body; stop it when the slow wears off. For frozen in ice use state.frozen, for dripping wet use state.wet, and for the one-off cast of a slow or time spell use magic.time.

effects.name: state.surprise
effects.whenToUse: A quick shocked or surprised reaction: an enemy spots the player, a pet is startled, a character gets a sudden fright or an unexpected gift, a jump scare, an alert in a stealth game. Play it at the head. For a lasting scare or panic use state.fear.

effects.name: state.thinking
effects.whenToUse: A character is thinking, pondering, waiting or loading: an NPC deciding, a customer choosing an order, an AI opponent taking its turn, a pet wondering, a puzzle hint about to appear. Follow the head; stop it when they decide. For sleeping or idling use state.sleep.

effects.name: state.ultready
effects.whenToUse: A hero's ultimate or special ability is charged and ready to use: the ult is up in a MOBA or hero shooter, a super meter is full, a special attack can be fired. Play it on the character (follow it) and stop it when the ability is used. For a character already blazing in a powered-up mode use state.aura.

effects.name: state.zerog
effects.whenToUse: A character or object is weightless: floating in zero gravity on a space station or a spacewalk, drifting in a low-gravity or anti-gravity zone, levitated by a gravity gun; follow the body and stop it when gravity returns (for underwater use env.bubbles, for a magical shimmer use state.sparkle).

effects.name: env.snow
effects.whenToUse: A winter level, a Christmas event, a cold mountain scene. Start it once when the level begins; it covers the whole screen.

effects.name: env.rain
effects.whenToUse: A rainy level, a storm, a sad scene. Start it once when the level begins; it covers the whole screen.

effects.name: env.leaves
effects.whenToUse: An autumn or forest level, a windy park, a garden. Tint pink for cherry blossom petals. Covers the whole screen from the top.

effects.name: env.embers
effects.whenToUse: A lava level, a burning city, a campfire scene, a volcano, a forge. Rises from the bottom of the screen.

effects.name: env.bubbles
effects.whenToUse: An underwater level, an aquarium, a soap or bath scene, a potion lab. Rises from the bottom of the screen.

effects.name: env.fog
effects.whenToUse: A spooky graveyard, a swamp, a morning meadow, a haunted house. Sits along the bottom of the screen and drifts sideways.

effects.name: env.stars
effects.whenToUse: A night sky, a space level, a dream sequence, a magic realm. Covers the whole screen; put it behind the game if you can (it is a background feel).

effects.name: env.fireflies
effects.whenToUse: A night forest, a fairy glade, a calm evening, a magical garden. Soft lights drifting everywhere.

effects.name: env.dust
effects.whenToUse: A sunlit room, an attic, a desert, a cave, an old library. Tiny motes drifting everywhere; very subtle.

effects.name: env.sandstorm
effects.whenToUse: A desert level, a dust storm, a windy wasteland. In 2D it blows left to right (dir 180 reverses). In 3D it blows along the ground: direction: [x, y, z], or dir as a compass heading (0 = +X, 90 = -Z).

effects.name: env.clouds
effects.whenToUse: A sky background, a flying level, a calm outdoor scene. Very slow; start it once. Play on the back layer if the game has a DOM scene.

effects.name: env.hearts
effects.whenToUse: A love scene, a date, a pet-care screen, a valentine event. Rises from the bottom of the screen.

effects.name: env.confetti
effects.whenToUse: A celebration screen that stays open: a winner podium, a birthday event, a season end. For a one-off burst use reward.confetti or reward.clear.

effects.name: env.storm
effects.whenToUse: A thunderstorm, a stormy night, a dramatic or scary level, bad weather in a day/night cycle. Play it once without a position for the whole screen (2D) or the area around the camera (3D); stop it when the storm passes. For calm rain use env.rain.

effects.name: env.spirits
effects.whenToUse: A haunted house, a graveyard, a cursed forest, a horror level, a spirit world or a dream. Play it once without a position for the whole screen (2D) or the area around the camera (3D); stop it to clear the air. For friendly night lights use env.fireflies.

effects.name: env.petals
effects.whenToUse: Spring, romance or peace: cherry blossom season, a Japanese or anime setting, a wedding, a love scene, a calm garden, a happy ending. Play it once without a position for the whole screen (2D) or the area around the camera (3D); stop it when the scene changes.

effects.name: env.blizzard
effects.whenToUse: A snowstorm: a frozen mountain, an arctic level, a harsh winter survival scene, a snow boss arena, a cold that should feel dangerous. Play it once without a position (whole screen in 2D, the area around the camera in 3D). For gentle snowfall use env.snow.

effects.name: env.ash
effects.whenToUse: A burning or ruined world: near a volcano, after an explosion or war, a city on fire, a post-apocalyptic wasteland, a dragon's lair, a hell level. Play it once without a position (whole screen in 2D, the area around the camera in 3D).

effects.name: env.meteors
effects.whenToUse: A magical or romantic night sky: a wish moment, a space level, a calm night camp, a dreamy menu background, a star festival. Play it once without a position; pair it with env.stars for a full starry sky.

effects.name: env.wind
effects.whenToUse: A windy place or a strong breeze: a cliff top, a sailing scene, a speed or flying level, a storm coming, a desert, a dramatic standoff. Play it once without a position. For a sandstorm use env.sandstorm; for snow in wind use env.blizzard.

effects.name: env.aurora
effects.whenToUse: A magical or arctic night sky with the northern lights (a snowy village at night, a polar level, a calm camp under the stars, a dreamy menu or ending); play it once without a position and it hangs across the top of the screen (in 3D above the spot the camera looks at), pair it with env.stars or env.snow, and use env.spirits for drifting ghost lights instead.

effects.name: env.christmas
effects.whenToUse: A Christmas or winter-holiday scene: a festive event, a Christmas level, shop or menu, a cosy snowy village, a gift-giving screen. Play it once without a position (whole screen in 2D, the area around the camera in 3D); tint it to recolour the lights. For plain snowfall use env.snow; for a snowstorm use env.blizzard.

effects.name: env.drizzle
effects.whenToUse: Light rain and a grey, gentle mood (a drizzly morning, a quiet town or forest, a calm or melancholy moment, the start or end of a shower); play it once without a position (whole screen in 2D, around the camera in 3D) and use env.rain for a proper downpour or env.storm for thunder and lightning.

effects.name: env.dustdevil
effects.whenToUse: A dry, hot, empty landscape where little dust whirls spin up now and then (a desert or wild-west town, a dusty road, a savanna or wasteland, a ghost-town standoff, a drought); play it once without a position (along the bottom of the screen in 2D, on the ground around the camera in 3D), set dir 180 in 2D to blow the breeze leftward or pass direction: [x, y, z] or a dir compass heading in 3D, and use magic.tornado for a whirlwind attack or env.sandstorm for a full storm.

effects.name: env.feathers
effects.whenToUse: Feathers floating in the air (a pillow fight, a bird flock or a scared chicken just passed, an angel or heaven scene, a peaceful dream, a bird-themed level); play it once without a position (whole screen in 2D, around the camera in 3D), tint it for coloured or dark crow feathers, and use env.leaves for leaves or env.petals for blossom petals.

effects.name: env.hail
effects.whenToUse: A hailstorm: ice pellets hammering down on a winter or mountain level, a freak storm, an ice boss arena or a weather hazard; play it once without a position (whole screen in 2D, around the camera in 3D) and use env.snow for soft snow, env.blizzard for a snowstorm or env.rain for rain.

effects.name: env.halloween
effects.whenToUse: A Halloween or spooky-fun event: a pumpkin patch, a trick-or-treat level, a witch's party, a haunted carnival, a costume or event menu. Play it once without a position (whole screen in 2D, the area around the camera in 3D). For a scary ghost atmosphere use env.spirits; for low fog use env.fog.

effects.name: env.heat
effects.whenToUse: Scorching heat (a desert at noon, a hot summer day, a sun-baked road or wasteland, a heatwave, the ground near a volcano or a furnace); play it once without a position (rising from the bottom of the screen in 2D, from the ground around the camera in 3D) and use env.sandstorm for blowing sand, env.embers for glowing embers or env.dust for plain floating dust.

effects.name: env.lanterns
effects.whenToUse: A calm festival night: a lantern festival, Diwali, Mid-Autumn or Lunar New Year, a wish or memorial moment, a romantic river or temple night, a peaceful ending. Play it once without a position (whole screen in 2D, the area around the camera in 3D). For small wandering lights use env.fireflies; for sparks from a fire use env.embers.

effects.name: env.magic
effects.whenToUse: An enchanted place or a magic mood: a fairy land, an enchanted forest, a wizard's tower, a magic shop, a dream world, a fantasy title screen or menu background. Play it once without a position for the whole screen (2D) or the area around the camera (3D); tint it to the world's magic colour. For a plain night sky use env.stars; for wandering firefly lights use env.fireflies; for spooky ghost lights use env.spirits.

effects.name: env.mist
effects.whenToUse: Creeping ghostly mist at floor level: a haunted crypt, a graveyard path at night, a spooky corridor, a witch's swamp, a horror level. Play it once without a position: it creeps along the bottom of the screen (2D, left to right; dir 180 reverses) or over the floor around the camera (3D: direction: [x, y, z], or dir as a compass heading). For a thick soft fog bank use env.fog; for floating ghost lights use env.spirits.

effects.name: env.nebula
effects.whenToUse: A colourful deep-space background for a space shooter, a space exploration level, a galaxy map or a cosmic menu: play it once without a position and keep it behind the game; for a plain starry night use env.stars, and add env.meteors for shooting stars.

effects.name: env.ocean
effects.whenToUse: By the sea (a beach, a harbour or pier, a ship deck, a pirate or sailing game, a lighthouse cliff, a surfing or fishing level); play it once without a position (over the lower part of the screen in 2D, around the camera in 3D), set dir 180 in 2D to blow the breeze leftward or pass direction: [x, y, z] or a dir compass heading in 3D, and use vehicle.wake for a boat's own wake, env.fog for still fog or env.wind for plain wind.

effects.name: env.partylights
effects.whenToUse: A party mood that stays on: a dance or rhythm game, a club or concert, a party room, a festival stage, a celebration menu or results background. Play it once without a position (whole screen in 2D, the area around the camera in 3D); stop it when the party ends. For a disco ball in the world use world.discoball; for falling confetti use env.confetti.

effects.name: env.pollen
effects.whenToUse: A calm sunny meadow or field: a summer or spring level, a farm, a picnic, a peaceful garden or a cosy outdoor menu background, with dandelion fluff and pollen floating slowly sideways and up. Play it once without a position for the whole screen (2D) or the area around the camera (3D); it drifts right (dir 180 drifts left). For falling blossom petals use env.petals; for indoor dust motes use env.dust; for lights at night use env.fireflies.

effects.name: env.rainbowsparkle
effects.whenToUse: A magical, happy or dreamy scene (a fairy or unicorn world, a candy land, a wish coming true, a princess or party menu, a rainbow level in a kids' game); play it once without a position (whole screen in 2D, around the camera in 3D), tint it for sparkles of one colour (no tint keeps the rainbow), and use env.confetti for party confetti or env.fireflies for floating fairy lights.

effects.name: env.smoke
effects.whenToUse: Smoke hanging in the air over a whole scene: a battlefield or war zone, a town after a battle, a siege, a forest burning in the distance, a smoky tavern or forge hall. Play it once without a position for the whole screen (2D) or the area around the camera (3D); it drifts left to right (dir 180 reverses; in 3D pass direction). For low spooky fog use env.fog; for falling ash use env.ash; for one thing smoking use state.smoke or weapon.smoke.

effects.name: env.space
effects.whenToUse: A space level where the ship keeps flying forward (space shooters, side-scrolling or vertical shmups, an asteroid run, a space race, a rocket menu screen): play it once without a position; the stars rush right to left by default, in 2D set dir (degrees, -90 = top to bottom for a vertical shooter); for a still, twinkling starry sky use env.stars, and add move.warp for a jump to hyperspace.

effects.name: env.spores
effects.whenToUse: A dark, magical place full of fungi (a glowing mushroom forest, a cave grotto, a swamp at night, an alien jungle, an enchanted wood); play it once without a position (rising from the bottom of the screen in 2D, from the ground around the camera in 3D) and use env.fireflies for wandering fireflies, env.embers for fire embers or env.dust for plain dust.

effects.name: env.sunrays
effects.whenToUse: Warm daylight mood: a forest clearing, morning or evening light, a church window, a dusty barn, a peaceful level, a heavenly moment. Play it once without a position for the whole screen (2D) or the area around the camera (3D); stop it at night.

effects.name: env.underground
effects.whenToUse: Under the earth (a cave, a mine shaft, a dungeon, a tunnel, a crypt, an ant nest, a creaky old ruin); play it once without a position (falling from the top of the screen in 2D, from above the area around the camera in 3D) and use env.dust for a calm sunlit room or env.spores for glowing mushroom spores.

effects.name: env.underwater
effects.whenToUse: An underwater level or scene: the sea floor, a coral reef, a sunken ship, a mermaid kingdom, a deep dive, the view inside an aquarium. Play it once without a position (whole screen in 2D, the area around the camera in 3D) and stop it when the player surfaces. For bubbles alone use env.bubbles; for bubbles from one spot use world.bubblecolumn.

effects.name: vehicle.exhaust
effects.whenToUse: A car, truck, motorbike or boat engine is running. Follow the exhaust pipe; in 3D pass direction (pointing backward out of the pipe) and keep it current with handle.aim(v) while the vehicle turns. Stop it when the engine stops.

effects.name: vehicle.nitro
effects.whenToUse: A car, kart, rocket or jetpack boosts: nitro, turbo, afterburner. Follow the exhaust or nozzle; in 3D pass direction (backward, out of the nozzle) and keep it current with handle.aim(v). Stop it when the boost ends.

effects.name: vehicle.crash
effects.whenToUse: Two cars collide, a car hits a wall or a pole, a vehicle lands hard or gets wrecked. Play it at the point of impact.

effects.name: vehicle.damaged
effects.whenToUse: A car, tank, plane or machine is badly damaged or wrecked: low health, a burning wreck, a broken generator. Follow the engine or hood; stop it when it is repaired or removed.

effects.name: vehicle.siren
effects.whenToUse: A police car, ambulance, fire truck or alarm is flashing: a chase, a crime or heist game, an emergency, a wanted level. Follow the light bar on the roof; stop it when the chase ends.

effects.name: vehicle.wake
effects.whenToUse: A boat, jet ski, surfboard or swimming creature moves through water. Follow the back of the hull at the water line; stop it when it stops. For a single splash use move.splash.

effects.name: vehicle.backfire
effects.whenToUse: A car, motorbike or hot rod backfires with a bang out of its exhaust (revving, shifting gear, a tuned engine, a cartoon car sputtering): play it once at the tailpipe, in 2D with dir (degrees, default 180 = left) and in 3D with direction pointing backward out of the pipe (for the steady smoke of a running engine use vehicle.exhaust, for a gun shot weapon.muzzle).

effects.name: vehicle.drift
effects.whenToUse: A car or kart is drifting sideways through a corner in a racing game. Follow a rear wheel (play one per wheel for both); in 2D set dir (degrees, default backward = left) and in 3D pass direction backward from the wheel. Stop it when the drift ends. Tint sets the spark colour (blue, orange, purple for kart drift-boost levels). For a short brake or a character sliding use move.skid; for the boost after the drift use vehicle.nitro.

effects.name: vehicle.explode
effects.whenToUse: A car, truck, tank, plane or other vehicle blows up and is destroyed: play it at the middle of the vehicle (for a crash without fire use vehicle.crash, for a fuel barrel explosion.barrel, for a bomb explosion.small, for a burning wreck afterwards use vehicle.damaged).

effects.name: vehicle.jump
effects.whenToUse: A car, truck, kart, bike or skateboard lands on the ground after a jump or ramp in a racing, stunt or monster-truck game. Play it under the wheels at the moment they touch down. Tint it for the ground (sand, snow, mud). For a vehicle hitting something use vehicle.crash; for a character landing use move.land.

effects.name: vehicle.offroad
effects.whenToUse: A car, truck, quad, dirt bike or tractor is driving fast over mud, dirt, sand or snow, spraying it up behind its wheels. Follow a rear wheel where it touches the ground; in 2D set dir (degrees, default 145 = backward and up for a vehicle driving right) and in 3D pass direction backward from the wheel and tilted up, keeping it current with handle.aim(v). Stop it when it stops or reaches a road. Tint it for the ground (brown mud, sand, snow). For light dust on a road use move.dust.

effects.name: vehicle.puddle
effects.whenToUse: A car, bike or kart drives through a puddle, a ford or a shallow stream, or a runner splashes through one at speed: play it once on the ground where the wheel hits the water, and tint it brown for a mud puddle (for something falling into water use move.splash, for a boat moving use vehicle.wake).

effects.name: vehicle.rotorwash
effects.whenToUse: A helicopter, drone, hovercraft or jet hovers low or lands and its rotor wind blasts the ground: play it on the ground under the rotor, keep it on the ground below the craft while it hovers (not up at the craft itself) and stop it when it lifts away (for one heavy landing use move.land, for a spinning wind attack magic.tornado).

effects.name: vehicle.scrape
effects.whenToUse: A car grinds along a wall or guard rail, a train brakes on its rails, a skateboard grinds a rail, a sword or plough drags on stone, a robot slides on metal: follow the point of contact, in 2D set dir (degrees, default 160 = back and up) and in 3D pass direction for where the sparks fly (backward along the car), and stop it when the contact ends (for one clang use hit.metal, for sparks from a broken machine world.sparks, for tyre smoke move.skid).

effects.name: vehicle.thruster
effects.whenToUse: A spaceship, drone, hover car, hover board, jetpack hover or robot thruster is running at cruising power: follow the nozzle with dir in 2D (degrees, default -90 = down; 180 for a ship flying right) or direction in 3D (out of the nozzle), keeping it current with handle.aim(v); for a roaring speed boost use vehicle.nitro, for a petrol engine use vehicle.exhaust.

effects.name: weapon.muzzle
effects.whenToUse: A gun, cannon or blaster fires: every shot. Play it at the barrel tip; in 2D set dir (degrees, 0 = right), in 3D pass direction along the barrel. Tiny and fast: fine at full-auto rates.

effects.name: weapon.smoke
effects.whenToUse: A smoke grenade, a smoke bomb, a flare canister, a fog machine or a coloured signal smoke. Play it on the ground where it landed; stop it after a few seconds and the cloud drifts away. Tint it for coloured smoke.

effects.name: weapon.laser
effects.whenToUse: A laser, blaster or energy bolt is fired in a shooter or shoot-em-up. Play it at the gun or ship nose; in 2D set dir (degrees: 90 = up for a vertical shooter, 0 = right), in 3D pass direction. It only shows the shot; for the hit use hit.bullet or hit.shieldzap.

effects.name: weapon.rocket
effects.whenToUse: A rocket, missile, RPG round, firework rocket or jetpack is flying. Follow the projectile; in 3D pass direction (backward, out of the tail) and keep it current with handle.aim(v). On impact stop it and play explosion.big.

effects.name: weapon.shell
effects.whenToUse: A gun ejects a spent casing after a shot (pair it with weapon.muzzle on every shot of a pistol, rifle or shotgun). Play it at the ejection port on the side of the gun; in 2D set dir (degrees) for the side the casing flies to.

effects.name: weapon.shotgun
effects.whenToUse: A shotgun, blunderbuss, cannon or scatter gun fires: one big spread shot. Play it at the barrel; in 2D set dir (degrees, 0 = right), in 3D pass direction along the barrel. For ordinary guns use weapon.muzzle.

effects.name: weapon.flamethrower
effects.whenToUse: A continuous stream of fire: a flamethrower, a dragon's breath, a fire hose of magic, a burning jet from a pipe. Play it at the nozzle or mouth; in 2D set dir (degrees), in 3D pass direction and keep it aimed with handle.aim(v). Stop it when the fire stops.

effects.name: weapon.arrowrain
effects.whenToUse: A volley of arrows rains down on an area: an archer tower or archer squad firing on a group, an arrow-rain skill in an RPG, tower defense or strategy game, a castle-siege volley. Play it on the ground at the centre of the target area (about 220 px wide at size 1); the arrows land from 0.4 s to 0.9 s. For a single arrow striking a target use hit.arrow; for a fireball from the sky use magic.meteor.

effects.name: weapon.boomerang
effects.whenToUse: A spinning thrown weapon is in flight: a boomerang, a chakram, a thrown axe or shuriken, a spinning saw blade, a returning shield or disc. Play it on the projectile with follow; stop it when it is caught or hits (then play hit.slash or hit.metal). For a projectile that does not spin use move.trail.

effects.name: weapon.cannon
effects.whenToUse: A cannon fires one heavy shot: a cannon tower in tower defense, a pirate ship broadside, a castle cannon, a tank gun. Play it at the muzzle; in 2D set dir (degrees, 0 = right), in 3D pass direction along the barrel. For ordinary guns use weapon.muzzle; for a spread of pellets use weapon.shotgun; where the shell lands use explosion.artillery.

effects.name: weapon.catapult
effects.whenToUse: A catapult, trebuchet, ballista or siege engine launches its load: the moment the arm swings in tower defense, castle siege and launch-the-boulder games. Play it at the top of the arm as it releases; in 2D set dir (degrees, the way the shot flies, default 60 = up and to the right), in 3D pass direction. Where the boulder lands use explosion.artillery.

effects.name: weapon.chargebow
effects.whenToUse: A ranged weapon is charging up before the shot: a bow being drawn, a charged arrow, a charge shot on a blaster, a slingshot pulled back, a power shot held. Play it at the arrow tip or barrel while the player holds; stop it on release and play the shot (move.trail on the flying arrow, weapon.laser or weapon.muzzle for a gun). For a hero charging a big energy attack in the hands use magic.charge, for casting a spell magic.cast.

effects.name: weapon.flamesword
effects.whenToUse: A weapon is on fire or fire-enchanted while it is held or swung: a flaming sword, a fire axe, a burning spear or club, a fire buff on the hero's blade. Play it on the blade with follow so flames and embers trail behind each swing; stop it when the enchantment ends. For a whole character on fire use state.burning, for a fireball in flight magic.fire, and for the blow landing hit.elementfire.

effects.name: weapon.frostblade
effects.whenToUse: A weapon is enchanted with ice or frost while it is held or swung: a frost sword, an ice axe, a freezing spear, a cold magic staff, an ice buff on the hero's blade. Play it on the blade with follow so mist and snowflakes trail behind each swing; stop it when the enchantment ends. For a frozen character use state.frozen, and for the blow landing hit.elementice.

effects.name: weapon.holyspear
effects.whenToUse: A weapon is holy, blessed or full of light while it is held or swung: a holy spear, a paladin's sword, a light lance, an angel's blade, a sacred staff, a legendary weapon shining. Play it on the weapon with follow; stop it when the blessing ends. For a holy spell burst use magic.holy, and for a blessing on a character magic.buff.

effects.name: weapon.launch
effects.whenToUse: A rocket launcher, bazooka, RPG, missile pod or recoilless cannon fires its round: play it once at the front of the tube, in 2D with dir (degrees, 0 = right; the backblast goes the opposite way) and in 3D with direction along the barrel, then follow the round with weapon.rocket (for a gun use weapon.muzzle, for a shotgun or cannon weapon.shotgun).

effects.name: weapon.minigun
effects.whenToUse: A minigun, gatling gun, machine-gun turret, mounted cannon or bullet-hell ship fires a continuous stream: play it at the barrel tip, in 2D with dir (degrees, 0 = right) and in 3D with direction along the barrel (keep it aimed with handle.aim(v) while the turret turns), and stop it when firing stops (for single shots use weapon.muzzle on each one, for a fire stream weapon.flamethrower).

effects.name: weapon.musket
effects.whenToUse: A musket, flintlock pistol, arquebus or old black-powder rifle fires: a pirate pistol, a redcoat line volley, a duel, a western or colonial shooter. Play it at the barrel tip; in 2D set dir (degrees, 0 = right), in 3D pass direction along the barrel. The big white smoke cloud is the point of it; for modern guns use weapon.muzzle, for a cannon use weapon.cannon, for a blunderbuss spread use weapon.shotgun.

effects.name: weapon.plasma
effects.whenToUse: A plasma gun, ion cannon, charged blaster or alien weapon fires a slow, heavy ball of energy (sci-fi shooters, space shmups, robot bosses): play it at the barrel with dir in 2D (degrees, 0 = right, 90 = up) or direction in 3D; for a thin, fast bolt use weapon.laser, and for the impact use hit.laser.

effects.name: weapon.poisondagger
effects.whenToUse: A weapon is coated in poison or venom while it is held or swung: a poisoned dagger, a venom blade, an acid sword, a toxic spear or arrowhead, a plague staff, a poison buff on the hero's weapon. Play it on the blade with follow; stop it when the coating wears off. For a poisoned character use state.poison, and for a poison splash landing magic.poison.

effects.name: weapon.railgun
effects.whenToUse: A railgun, sniper beam, gauss rifle or charged hitscan shot fires and instantly reaches far (sci-fi shooters, space games, mech battles): play it at the barrel with dir in 2D (degrees, 0 = right, 90 = up) or direction in 3D; for a bolt that travels use weapon.laser, for a long beam held for half a second use magic.beam.

effects.name: weapon.thunderhammer
effects.whenToUse: A weapon crackles with lightning while it is held or swung: a thunder hammer, a lightning sword, a shock spear, an electric baton or a storm staff, an electric buff on the hero's weapon. Play it on the weapon's head with follow; stop it when the charge ends. For a whole character being shocked use state.electrified, and for the blow landing hit.elementshock.

effects.name: weapon.torpedo
effects.whenToUse: A torpedo, underwater missile, submarine drone or anything with a propeller speeding under water. Follow its tail; in 2D set dir to the way the trail streams out (degrees, default 180 = to the left, for a torpedo heading right); in 3D pass direction (backward, out of the tail) and keep it current with handle.aim(v). On impact stop it and play explosion.water. For a missile in the air use weapon.rocket; for a boat on the surface use vehicle.wake.

effects.name: weapon.tractorbeam
effects.whenToUse: A UFO or spaceship beams something up: an alien abduction, a ship lifting cows, crates or the player, a pickup beam pulling loot aboard; play it under the saucer and follow it (the beam hangs about 220 px down; in 2D dir in degrees turns it, default -90 = down), and stop it when the beam switches off (for a beam marking dropped loot use world.lootbeam, for a beam attack use magic.beam).

effects.name: gather.wood
effects.whenToUse: An axe hits a tree, a log is chopped, wood is harvested or a wooden thing is hacked at. Play it at the spot that was hit, once per swing; for a wooden crate breaking use hit.block.

effects.name: gather.stone
effects.whenToUse: A pickaxe hits rock, ore or a wall; stone is mined or quarried; a boulder is chipped. Play it where it was struck, once per swing. Tint it for ore colours (gold, iron, crystal).

effects.name: gather.harvest
effects.whenToUse: A crop, fruit, flower or plant is harvested or picked: farming games, pulling a carrot, picking an apple, collecting herbs, a garden plot ready. Play it on the plant at the moment it is picked.

effects.name: gather.drill
effects.whenToUse: A drill, jackhammer, mining laser or digging machine bores into rock, ore, concrete or a wall: play it where the bit touches, in 2D with dir (degrees, default 90 = chips fly up out of the hole) and in 3D with direction pointing out of the hole, tint it for ore colours and stop it when drilling stops (for one pickaxe swing use gather.stone, for cutting wood world.saw).

effects.name: gather.egg
effects.whenToUse: A hen lays an egg or an egg is collected in a farm or animal game: picking eggs from a nest, a coop producing, a bird laying, an egg-hunt find. Play it on the egg. For picking crops use gather.harvest; for a generic item pickup use pickup.sparkle.

effects.name: gather.fish
effects.whenToUse: A fish or anything else is pulled out of the water: a catch in a fishing game, a fish on the hook reeled in, a net hauled up, treasure or junk fished out. Play it on the water surface where it comes out; tint it with the catch's rarity colour (gold, purple, blue). For a plain splash use move.splash; for a bobber waiting in the water use world.ripple.

effects.name: gather.seed
effects.whenToUse: A seed, sapling or bulb is planted or sown in a farming or garden game: tapping an empty plot, placing a crop, sowing a field tile. Play it on the soil where it goes in. For picking a grown crop use gather.harvest; for a shovel digging or a hit into the ground use hit.dirt.

effects.name: gather.water
effects.whenToUse: A plant, crop, flower bed or garden plot is being watered with a watering can in a farming or garden game. Play it on the soil at the plant's base and stop it when watering ends; the water pours in from a can held up to the left (dir: 180 pours from the right instead). For a fountain or a broken pipe use world.fountain; for rain use env.rain.

effects.name: world.campfire
effects.whenToUse: A campfire, bonfire, fireplace, brazier, burning barrel or a torch in the world. Play it on the fire's base and leave it running; size 0.5 makes a torch or candle-sized flame.

effects.name: world.beacon
effects.whenToUse: Marks a place the player must go: a quest objective, a waypoint, a delivery drop-off, a mission start, the next checkpoint. Play it on the ground at that spot and stop it when the player arrives (then play reward.checkpoint).

effects.name: world.lootbeam
effects.whenToUse: Marks dropped loot, a weapon on the ground, an airdrop or a rare item so it can be seen from afar (battle royale, RPG, looter). Play it on the item and stop it when picked up. Tint by rarity: white common, green uncommon, blue rare, purple epic, gold legendary.

effects.name: world.build
effects.whenToUse: A building, wall, tower, furniture or block is placed or finishes construction: base building, city builders, sandbox and voxel games, tower defense placement, an upgrade completing. Play it at the base of the new thing; size it to the building (size 2 for a house).

effects.name: world.torch
effects.whenToUse: A wall torch, a hand-held torch, a lantern flame, a candle (size 0.4), a brazier in a dungeon, castle or cave. Play it where the flame sits on top of the torch and leave it running; follow a carried torch.

effects.name: world.fountain
effects.whenToUse: A water fountain in a town square or garden, a geyser, a broken water pipe, a whale's spout, a magic spring. Play it at the nozzle and leave it running.

effects.name: world.lava
effects.whenToUse: A pool or river of lava, a bubbling cauldron of fire, a volcano crater, molten metal in a forge, a hazard floor. Play it at the centre of the pool and leave it running; size it to the pool (size 2 for a big one).

effects.name: world.steam
effects.whenToUse: Steam or vapour escaping: a pipe or vent in a factory, a hot spring, a boiling pot or kettle, a geyser vent, a cooling engine, hot food. Play it at the opening and leave it running; size 0.4 for a cup or pot.

effects.name: world.sparks
effects.whenToUse: Something sparks on and off: a torn power cable, a damaged machine or robot, a short circuit, a grinder or welding, a broken street light, a sci-fi corridor. Play it at the break and leave it running.

effects.name: world.crystal
effects.whenToUse: A magic crystal, gem cluster, power core, energy stone or glowing ore in the world: cave crystals, a mana well, a sci-fi reactor core, a collectible that should catch the eye. Play it on the crystal and leave it running.

effects.name: world.ripple
effects.whenToUse: Something disturbs still water over time: a fishing bobber, a duck or frog sitting in a pond, a drip into a puddle, a stone just dropped in, something swimming under the surface. Play it on the water surface and leave it running; for one big splash use move.splash.

effects.name: world.boostpad
effects.whenToUse: A speed boost pad, a jump ramp marker, a conveyor or launch strip in a racing, runner or platform game: anything that says "go this way, fast". Play it on the pad; in 2D set dir (degrees, 0 = right), in 3D it lies on the ground pointing along +X (turn the pad, not the effect). When something drives over it play vehicle.nitro.

effects.name: world.altar
effects.whenToUse: A cursed altar, an evil brazier, a demon shrine, a witch's cauldron fire, a ritual candle stand or a dark-magic beacon in a dungeon, temple or haunted level. Play it where the flames sit on top of the altar and leave it running. For an ordinary warm fire use world.campfire or world.torch; for an altar or table enchanting an item use world.enchant.

effects.name: world.anvil
effects.whenToUse: A blacksmith hammers hot metal on an anvil, a forge or crafting station makes or upgrades an item, a weapon is reforged, a horseshoe is struck: play it once per hammer blow on the anvil (for metal hitting metal in a fight use hit.metal, for sparks that keep going world.sparks).

effects.name: world.banner
effects.whenToUse: A proud victory banner or war standard shedding gold in the wind: a regiment's standard carried into battle, a kingdom or guild banner on a castle wall, a champion's banner on a victory or rank screen. Play it on the cloth and leave it running (follow it when it is carried); the gold streams off downwind, to the right by default (dir 180 sends it left). For a flag a team has captured or holds use world.flag; for the troops inspired around it use state.rally.

effects.name: world.bloom
effects.whenToUse: A flower blooms or a plant grows in the world: a seed sprouts in a farming or garden game, a flower opens, a bush or tree finishes growing, a garden plot is planted, a dead plant comes back to life. Play it on the plant at that moment; tint it to the flower colour. For a plant that keeps growing over time use world.grow; for a nature spell use magic.nature; for picking a crop use gather.harvest.

effects.name: world.bubblecolumn
effects.whenToUse: Bubbles rise steadily from one spot under water: a vent or crack in the sea floor, a diver's or submarine's air, a fish-tank air stone, a sunken treasure chest, a hidden cave entrance, a bubbling swamp. Play it at the source and leave it running. For bubbles over the whole screen use env.bubbles; for a swimming character use move.swim.

effects.name: world.burning
effects.whenToUse: A building, house, tent, hut, barn, wooden tower, ship or siege engine is on fire: a raided village, a burning castle or camp in a strategy game, a house fire for firefighters. Play it at the base of the building and leave it running; size 1 fits a tent or hut, size 2 a house. For a small campfire or brazier use world.campfire; for a burning character or object use state.burning; for chimney smoke use world.chimney.

effects.name: world.capture
effects.whenToUse: A capture point or control zone in strategy, MOBA, arena or shooter games: king of the hill, a point being captured, a zone a team holds. Play it on the ground at the zone's centre, size it to the zone, tint it with the capturing team's colour and stop it when the capture ends (then play reward.checkpoint). For a place the player must walk to use world.beacon; for a healing area use magic.heallaura.

effects.name: world.cauldron
effects.whenToUse: A witch's cauldron or potion pot bubbling: brewing a potion, an alchemy or crafting station, a magic soup, a bubbling vat of slime in a lab. Play it on the liquid's surface and leave it running; tint it to the potion colour. For lava or molten metal use world.lava; for food frying in a pan use world.cooking.

effects.name: world.chestidle
effects.whenToUse: An unopened treasure chest, loot crate or reward box sits in the level waiting to be found or opened (a dungeon chest, a hidden chest, a daily chest on the map); play it on the chest and leave it running, stop it and play reward.chest when it opens, and use state.sparkle for any other item that wants attention.

effects.name: world.chimney
effects.whenToUse: Smoke rising from a chimney or smokestack that stays in place: a cosy cottage or cabin roof, a village house in winter, a factory or power-plant stack, a steam train funnel, a blacksmith's forge. Play it on the top of the chimney and leave it running; it drifts right (dir 180 drifts left; in 3D pass direction or dir as a compass heading). For something damaged and smoking use state.smoke; for white steam from a vent use world.steam; for a campfire use world.campfire.

effects.name: world.cooking
effects.whenToUse: Food is frying or sizzling: a pan or wok on the stove, a grill or barbecue, a griddle or hot plate in a cooking or restaurant game. Play it on the cooking surface and leave it running while the food cooks. For a boiling pot or kettle use world.steam; for a bubbling potion pot use world.cauldron.

effects.name: world.crumble
effects.whenToUse: A crumbling platform, cracked ledge, rotten bridge plank or stone floor breaks and falls away under the player in a platformer or dungeon; play it at the middle of the platform, size it to the platform width and tint it the colour of the stone or wood, and use hit.block for a crate or wall smashed by a hit or explosion.dust for a whole building collapsing.

effects.name: world.datastream
effects.whenToUse: Data streams upward in a cyber world (a server rack, a data pillar or terminal, a cyberspace level, a computer core, an upload in progress, a hacker hideout): play it at the base and leave it running; for a hologram projector use world.hologram, for a teleporter pad use world.teleporter.

effects.name: world.discoball
effects.whenToUse: A disco ball over a dance floor: a party room, nightclub, roller disco, prom, a dance or rhythm game stage. Play it on the ball (it hangs above the floor) and leave it running; in 3D the light spots sweep over the floor below. For soft coloured party glows over the whole screen use env.partylights.

effects.name: world.dooropen
effects.whenToUse: A door, gate, portcullis, vault or dungeon entrance in the level opens and shows the way on (after a key, a switch or a cleared room); play it at the middle of the doorway and size it to the door, and use world.keyhole for the key turning in the lock or magic.portal for a warp gate.

effects.name: world.dripping
effects.whenToUse: Water dripping on its own from above: a cave ceiling or stalactite, a leaky pipe or tap, a wet rock, a melting icicle, a sewer or dungeon. Play it where the drop forms (the ceiling or the pipe end), about 120 px above the floor at size 1; size scales the fall. For rings on a water surface use world.ripple; for rain use env.rain; for a jet of water use world.fountain.

effects.name: world.enchant
effects.whenToUse: An item is being enchanted, imbued or infused with magic: an enchanting table or altar at work, a weapon receiving a rune, a gem being socketed, magic crafting in progress. Play it on the item and stop it when done (then play reward.upgrade, or hit.upgradefail if it failed). For a character charging a spell use magic.cast; for a glowing crystal in the level use world.crystal.

effects.name: world.flag
effects.whenToUse: A flag, banner or standard that has been captured or is held: capture the flag, a team banner on a conquered tower or castle, a flag raised on a won base. Play it on the flag cloth and stop it when the flag is lost; tint it with the owning team's colour. For the moment of capture play reward.checkpoint; for the zone being captured use world.capture.

effects.name: world.forcefield
effects.whenToUse: A force-field wall or energy door blocks a doorway, gate or corridor in a sci-fi level (a locked door, a barrier the player must switch off, a containment cell, a safe-zone wall): play it at the centre of the opening (size 1 is about 120 x 150 px) and stop it when the field goes down; for a dome around a character or base use state.dome, for a hit on the field use hit.shieldzap.

effects.name: world.grave
effects.whenToUse: A haunted grave, a tombstone, a crypt door, a cursed burial mound or a spooky spot in a graveyard where something might rise. Play it on the ground at the grave and leave it running. For ghost lights over the whole level use env.spirits; for the undead climbing out once use magic.raise.

effects.name: world.grow
effects.whenToUse: A plant, crop, tree or flower is growing over time: a farm plot between planting and harvest, a sapling sprouting, a fertilised field, a magic beanstalk. Play it at the base of the plant and leave it running until it is ready. For a one-off growth spell use magic.nature; for health regenerating use state.regen.

effects.name: world.hologram
effects.whenToUse: A hologram, holo-display or projector is on in a sci-fi level (a mission briefing table, a holo-map, a shop terminal, a ghostly AI guide, a projected character): play it at the projector and leave it running, drawing the projected picture yourself on top; for a beam marking dropped loot use world.lootbeam, for a teleporter pad use world.teleporter.

effects.name: world.keyhole
effects.whenToUse: A key the player carries is used on a lock (a locked door, chest, gate or padlock in an adventure, dungeon or escape-room game); play it on the lock, then world.dooropen or reward.chest for what opens, and use pickup.key for picking the key up or ui.unlock for an unlock on a menu screen.

effects.name: world.laserfence
effects.whenToUse: A laser fence, laser tripwire or security laser grid blocks a gap between two posts (a heist or stealth level, a prison cell, a sci-fi checkpoint, a hazard the player must not touch): play it at the middle of the gap (size 1 spans about 160 px) and stop it when the lasers switch off; for a single laser shot use weapon.laser, for a solid energy wall use world.forcefield.

effects.name: world.planetring
effects.whenToUse: A ringed planet, an asteroid belt around a moon or a space station, a debris ring circling a boss or a space base in a space game: play it at the planet's centre and leave it running (a flat ring about 240 px across: seen from above in 2D, lying level around the centre in 3D); for one satellite circling a character use move.orbit.

effects.name: world.pressureplate
effects.whenToUse: A pressure plate, floor button or weight switch is stepped on or pressed down by a crate in a platformer, dungeon or puzzle level; play it on the plate at floor level, and use world.switch for a lever or wall button, world.trap for a hidden trap that fires, or move.land for a plain heavy landing.

effects.name: world.rally
effects.whenToUse: A rally point, move order or gather point for units in RTS, tower defense and tactics games: where troops will walk to or gather. Play it on the ground at the point and stop it when the units arrive or the order changes. For a one-tap acknowledgement use ui.tap; for a quest objective the player must reach use world.beacon.

effects.name: world.reactor
effects.whenToUse: A glowing reactor, power core, generator or energy engine runs in a sci-fi level (a ship's engine room, a power plant, a boss's power source, a fusion core to protect or destroy, a mech's chest core): play it on the core and leave it running; for a magic crystal or gem use world.crystal, for a sparking broken machine use world.sparks.

effects.name: world.savepoint
effects.whenToUse: A save point, rest spot, respawn pad or healing station that stays active in an RPG, platformer or adventure level; play it on the ground at the spot and leave it running, play reward.checkpoint once when the player actually saves or touches it, and use world.beacon for a "go here" objective marker.

effects.name: world.saw
effects.whenToUse: A saw, chainsaw, sawmill, wood lathe or sanding machine cuts wood, or a carpenter or crafting bench is working: play it where the blade meets the wood, in 2D with dir (degrees, default 17 = right and a little up) and in 3D with direction for where the dust flies, tint it for darker wood and stop it when cutting stops (for an axe chop use gather.wood, for drilling rock gather.drill).

effects.name: world.scanner
effects.whenToUse: A scanning beam sweeps up and down over something (a security scanner at a gate, a body or item scan, a sci-fi checkpoint, a drone scanning the player, an analysis or cloning station): play it at the feet or base of what is scanned (size 1 covers a character) and stop it when the scan is done; for a hologram projector use world.hologram, for a teleporter pad use world.teleporter.

effects.name: world.secret
effects.whenToUse: A secret is discovered in the level (a hidden room, a fake wall, a secret passage or a hidden collectible revealed in a platformer, dungeon or adventure game); play it where the secret appears, and use ui.unlock for something unlocked on a menu screen or world.dooropen for an ordinary door opening.

effects.name: world.shore
effects.whenToUse: Gentle surf along a beach or lake shore: foam lapping at the water's edge on a tropical island, a beach resort, a lakeside camp, a river bank, a calm sea. Play it on the water line and leave it running; the line runs left to right (in 3D along the X axis), size 2 makes it twice as long. For waves crashing on rocks use world.wave; for a boat's foam use vehicle.wake.

effects.name: world.smelt
effects.whenToUse: A furnace, smelter, forge, kiln, oven or blacksmith hearth is working: ore being smelted, metal heating, a crafting station busy in an idle, factory or survival game. Play it at the furnace opening and leave it running; stop it when the fire goes out. For an open campfire use world.campfire; for a pool of molten metal use world.lava.

effects.name: world.spawnportal
effects.whenToUse: The place enemies come out of in tower defense, wave survival or horde games: an enemy spawn point, a demon rift, a monster gate on the ground. Play it on the ground at the spawn and leave it running; play move.spawn as each enemy appears. For a friendly portal, warp gate or level exit use magic.portal.

effects.name: world.speaker
effects.whenToUse: A loudspeaker, boombox, jukebox, stage or DJ booth plays music in the world: a party, a concert, a dance club, a radio in a room. Play it on the speaker and leave it running; stop it when the music stops. For notes around a singing or listening character use state.music.

effects.name: world.spikes
effects.whenToUse: A spike trap fires out of the floor in a platformer, dungeon or obstacle course (floor spikes, a spike pit, retracting blades popping up); play it on the ground where the spikes come out, and use magic.earth for rock spikes from a spell or world.trap for a trap with no spikes.

effects.name: world.sprinkler
effects.whenToUse: A lawn or garden sprinkler, an irrigation sprayer on a farm, a splash pad in a water park, a park water feature. Play it on the sprinkler head on the ground and leave it running. For a single jet straight up use world.fountain; for a leaking pipe use world.dripping.

effects.name: world.switch
effects.whenToUse: A lever, wall switch, crank or big button in the level is flipped or pressed (opening a gate, starting a machine, lighting a puzzle path); play it on the switch, and use world.pressureplate for a plate the player steps on, world.keyhole for a key in a lock or ui.tap for a button on the screen.

effects.name: world.teleporter
effects.whenToUse: A teleporter pad, warp gate on the floor, jump pad to another level, sci-fi elevator or beam-me-up spot stands ready in the level: play it on the pad and leave it running, and play move.teleport on whoever steps in; for a quest marker use world.beacon, for a hologram projector use world.hologram.

effects.name: world.towerup
effects.whenToUse: A tower, turret, building or unit is upgraded to its next level in tower defense, city builder, idle or merge games. Play it at the base of the thing as the upgrade lands; size it to the building. For a new building being placed use world.build; for the player levelling up use reward.levelup; for a character's stat boost use magic.buff.

effects.name: world.trap
effects.whenToUse: A hidden trap is triggered in a dungeon, platformer or adventure level (a bear trap snaps shut, a tripwire or floor trap fires, a pit trap or snare springs); play it on the ground where it fires and tint it for the floor (sand, snow, stone), and use world.spikes for spikes shooting out of the floor or explosion.mine for a mine that explodes.

effects.name: world.volcano
effects.whenToUse: A volcano erupting in the world: a volcano island or level, a lava boss arena, a dinosaur or prehistoric scene, a fire mountain in the background, a crater spewing molten rock. Play it on the crater and leave it running; size 2-3 for a volcano in the background. For a pool of lava use world.lava; for ash falling over the whole screen use env.ash; for one fire ball from the sky use magic.meteor.

effects.name: world.waterfall
effects.whenToUse: Where a waterfall, a weir, a dam spillway or a pouring pipe crashes into the water or rocks below: a jungle or forest level, a river, a cliff pool, a water park. Play it at the bottom of the falling water and leave it running; size 2 for a big fall. For a jet shooting up use world.fountain; for one splash use move.splash; for calm rings on a pond use world.ripple.

effects.name: world.wave
effects.whenToUse: Waves keep crashing against rocks, a cliff, a pier, a breakwater or a beach: a coastal level, a lighthouse, a harbour, a pirate island, a stormy sea. Play it where the water hits and leave it running. For calm foam lapping along a beach use world.shore; for one big splash use explosion.water.

effects.name: world.whirlpool
effects.whenToUse: A whirlpool, maelstrom or drain swirls on the water: a sea hazard that pulls boats in, a plug-hole draining a bath or sink, a vortex in a river, a sea monster about to rise, a water portal. Play it at the centre on the water surface and leave it running; it is seen from above (in 3D it lies flat on the water). For a magic or space vortex use magic.blackhole; for a tornado use magic.tornado.

effects.name: world.wormhole
effects.whenToUse: A wormhole, space tunnel or hyperspace gate hanging in space: a jump point between sectors, a sci-fi level exit, a time tunnel, a shortcut in a space race; play it at its centre and leave it running, facing the viewer (for a magic portal or warp gate use magic.portal, for something that pulls things in use magic.blackhole, for a ship jumping away use move.warp).

effects.name: puzzle.match
effects.whenToUse: A tile, gem, candy or block is cleared in a match-3, a tile puzzle, a bubble shooter or a sorting game. Play it on each cleared tile (el: the tile, or at its centre); tint it with the tile's colour. Cheap enough for a whole cascade at once.

effects.name: puzzle.line
effects.whenToUse: A full row or column is cleared: a line clear in a block puzzle or tetris-like, a striped candy, a row bonus. Play it on the row with el: the row element, or at its centre with width: the row length in px. For a column set dir: 90.

effects.name: puzzle.shatter
effects.whenToUse: A gem, crystal, ice block or glass tile breaks: a locked or frozen tile freed in a puzzle, a crystal smashed, a glass obstacle broken. Tint it with the gem's colour.

effects.name: puzzle.merge
effects.whenToUse: Two or more items combine into a better one: a merge game (2048, merge dragons, suika), fusing, crafting two things together, a level-up of a unit. Play it where the new item appears; tint it with the new item's colour.

effects.name: puzzle.blast
effects.whenToUse: A special tile, bomb or booster fires in a match-3 or block puzzle: a cross blast that clears a row and a column, a bomb candy, a rocket booster. Play it on the special tile.

effects.name: puzzle.wrong
effects.whenToUse: The player makes a wrong or invalid move: a wrong answer in a quiz or logic puzzle, a swap that makes no match, a locked tile tapped, a mistake in a sorting or word game. Play it on the tile or answer; keep the sound short too.

effects.name: puzzle.hint
effects.whenToUse: Show the player what to do next: a hint on a tile, the next move in a tutorial, an idle nudge after a few seconds, a clickable item in a hidden-object game. Play it on the tile (el: the tile) and stop it when the player acts.

effects.name: puzzle.bubble
effects.whenToUse: A bubble pops: a bubble shooter match, a balloon popped, a soap bubble tapped, a slime ball burst, a pop-it toy. Play it on each bubble; tint it with the bubble's colour. Cheap enough for many at once.

effects.name: ui.pop
effects.whenToUse: A button, card or toggle is tapped. Small and quick; safe to fire on every tap. Play with { el }.

effects.name: ui.tap
effects.whenToUse: Feedback for a tap on the game itself: placing, selecting, moving to a point. Play with { event }.

effects.name: ui.star
effects.whenToUse: A star on a result screen is earned, a rating star fills, a favourite is marked. Play with { el } on the star.

effects.name: ui.burst
effects.whenToUse: A reward is claimed, a task is checked off, a purchase completes, a gift is opened in the UI. Play with { el }.

effects.name: ui.unlock
effects.whenToUse: A level, skin, character or feature unlocks; a lock icon opens; a new area is revealed. Play with { el }.

effects.name: ui.flash
effects.whenToUse: A screen flash: a huge explosion, a lightning strike, a camera flash, a big hit on the player (tint red), a teleport. Covers the whole screen for a moment.

effects.name: ui.glow
effects.whenToUse: Draw the eye to a button or card: Play, Claim, a ready chest, a new item. Play with { el, follow: true }; stop when tapped.

effects.name: ui.shine
effects.whenToUse: Draw attention to a button, card or banner with a passing shine: Play, Claim, a new offer. Play with { el }; the sweep fits the element width.

effects.name: ui.countup
effects.whenToUse: A score, coin total or XP bar is counting up on a result screen. Play with { el, follow: true } on the counter; stop when the count finishes.

effects.name: ui.achievement
effects.whenToUse: An achievement or badge unlocks in the UI: a quest completed, a milestone reached, a daily goal met, an achievement pop-up appearing. Play it with { el } on the badge icon; it fits the badge size. For a cup or trophy won in a tournament use reward.trophy; for a rank or league promotion use reward.rankup; for a level, skin or feature unlocking use ui.unlock.

effects.name: ui.beat
effects.whenToUse: A beat indicator that pulses once a second: the hit zone or beat bar of a rhythm game, a button to tap in time, a metronome, a heartbeat-timed prompt. Play with { el, follow: true } on the button or the beat bar; stop it when the music stops. For a plain attention glow use ui.glow.

effects.name: ui.carddeal
effects.whenToUse: A card is dealt, drawn, played or slid onto the table in a card, solitaire, poker or deck-building game: play it where the card lands and set dir (degrees, on screen, also in 3D) to the way the card travelled (default right). For turning a card face up use ui.cardflip.

effects.name: ui.cardflip
effects.whenToUse: A card is flipped face up or turned over during play in a memory-match, solitaire or card game, or a hidden tile is turned; light enough for every flip. Play it with { el } on the card as it turns. For a prize, gacha or card-pack reveal on a reward screen use reward.cardreveal; for a card being dealt use ui.carddeal.

effects.name: ui.chip
effects.whenToUse: Casino or poker chips are placed, bet, stacked or won at a table: a bet in blackjack, roulette or poker, a pot pushed to the winner. Play it on the chip stack and tint it with the chip colour. For coins collected use pickup.coin; for a big casino win use reward.jackpot.

effects.name: ui.cooldown
effects.whenToUse: An ability, skill or item button comes off cooldown and can be used again: a spell icon in a MOBA, a skill button in an action RPG, a dash or grenade button in a shooter. Play with { el } on the button. For a button that keeps glowing until tapped use ui.glow.

effects.name: ui.correct
effects.whenToUse: A correct answer in a quiz, trivia, spelling, maths or kids learning game: the right card, word, number or picture is chosen. Play it with { el } on the answer; the ring and sparkles fit its size. For a wrong answer use puzzle.wrong (or ui.wrongtry for a gentle try-again); for a reward being claimed use ui.burst.

effects.name: ui.countdown
effects.whenToUse: A countdown tick before a round or race starts: play it once on each 3, 2, 1 number, or on each of the last seconds of a timer running out. Play with { el } on the number. For the final GO! use ui.go.

effects.name: ui.dice
effects.whenToUse: Dice are rolled or land in a board, ludo, snakes-and-ladders, yahtzee, backgammon or casino game: play it on each die as it settles (el: the die), or where the roll lands. For a token moving on the board use ui.tap; for a big lucky win use reward.jackpot.

effects.name: ui.fill
effects.whenToUse: A progress, XP, loading or quest bar fills up or completes: a level-progress bar reaching the end, a battle-pass tier done, an upgrade or build finishing. Play with { el } on the bar, or at its centre with width and height (the bar size in px); the sweep fits its width. For a number counting up use ui.countup; for a glint passing over a button use ui.shine.

effects.name: ui.focuslines
effects.whenToUse: A dramatic manga moment over the whole screen: a critical or finishing hit, a special move starting, a boss appearing, a big surprise or reveal. Play it once with no position; it frames the middle of the screen. For a white screen flash use ui.flash; for the hit itself use hit.crit; for outward lines while moving fast use ui.speedlines.

effects.name: ui.frozen
effects.whenToUse: The player is frozen or freezing, shown on the whole screen: hit by a frost attack, caught in a freeze trap, standing in a cold zone or a blizzard. Start it once with no position (frost creeps into the corners of the whole screen) and stop it when they thaw. For a frozen character or enemy use state.frozen; for an ice hit use hit.ice.

effects.name: ui.gameover
effects.whenToUse: The player loses: game over, out of lives, time up, defeat, mission failed. Play it once with no position as the game-over screen appears: the edges of the whole screen darken with smoke and ash drifts down. For a character being knocked out use hit.ko; for a win use ui.victory.

effects.name: ui.go
effects.whenToUse: The race, round or match starts: the GO! after a 3-2-1 countdown, a "Start!" or "Fight!" banner, the first moment of a hypercasual level. Play with { el } on the GO text or at the centre of the screen. For the 3-2-1 ticks use ui.countdown; for a win use reward.confetti.

effects.name: ui.hack
effects.whenToUse: A hack, code crack or terminal breach succeeds in the UI (a lock picked in a hacking minigame, a password cracked, a firewall broken, a system unlocked, a cyber puzzle solved): play it with { el } on the panel, lock or button; for an ordinary unlock use ui.unlock, for a pixel-art explosion use explosion.pixel.

effects.name: ui.healed
effects.whenToUse: The player is healed, shown on the whole screen: a health potion drunk, a med kit used, health refilled at a checkpoint, a campfire or between waves. Play it once with no position: it rises from the bottom of the whole screen. For the heal effect on the character itself use magic.heal; for health ticking up over time use state.regen.

effects.name: ui.hurry
effects.whenToUse: Time is running out: the last seconds of a level timer, a countdown about to end, a bomb about to blow in a puzzle, a turn timer almost done. Play with { el, follow: true } on the timer and stop it when time is up or added. For a one-off tick on each 3, 2, 1 number use ui.countdown; for a single whole-screen warning flash use ui.flash with a red tint.

effects.name: ui.hurt
effects.whenToUse: The player takes damage: hit by an enemy, a trap, a bullet, a fall or a bad item; play it on every hit the player character takes. Play it once with no position: it reddens the edges of the whole screen and leaves the middle clear. For a full white screen flash use ui.flash; for the hit on the character itself use hit.impact; for a heart icon lost in the HUD use ui.lifelost; for a lasting low-health warning use ui.lowhp.

effects.name: ui.levelstart
effects.whenToUse: A level, stage, round or wave begins: play it once with no position as the level appears, and a band of light sweeps across the whole screen. For a screen change that hides a swap of screens use ui.transition; for the GO! after a 3-2-1 countdown use ui.go; for a shine across one button use ui.shine; for finishing a level use reward.clear.

effects.name: ui.lifelost
effects.whenToUse: The player loses a life or a heart in the HUD: a hit that costs a life, a failed try, a wrong answer that takes a heart, one less retry. Play with { el } on the heart icon as it is removed. For a heart being collected use pickup.heart; for the hit on the character itself use hit.impact.

effects.name: ui.lowhp
effects.whenToUse: The player is on low health or close to dying: start it when health drops under about a quarter and stop it when they heal or die. Play it once with no position: it beats at the edges of the whole screen. For a single hit use ui.hurt.

effects.name: ui.miss
effects.whenToUse: A missed note or beat in a rhythm game, a tap that came too late, a timing window lost in a tapping or timing game. Play it on the note lane or the tap spot; it deflates gently instead of scolding. For a wrong answer or an invalid move use puzzle.wrong.

effects.name: ui.new
effects.whenToUse: Mark a button, item or card as new or not yet seen: a new skin or item in the shop, a freshly unlocked level or mode, an unread tab, a just-added feature. Play with { el, follow: true } on it and stop it when the player opens it. For a pulsing glow behind a call-to-action use ui.glow; for sparkles circling a special offer use ui.sparkle; for the moment something unlocks use ui.unlock.

effects.name: ui.notify
effects.whenToUse: A notification lands on an icon, tab or menu button: a new message, a mission ready to claim, a gift waiting, a friend request. Play with { el } on the icon (the dot pops at its top-right corner) or on a small badge (it pops in the middle); without an element pass width and height (the icon size in px). For drawing the eye to a button use ui.glow; for marking an unseen item use ui.new.

effects.name: ui.poisoned
effects.whenToUse: The player is poisoned or sick, shown on the whole screen: a poison or gas attack, a toxic swamp or radiation zone, a bad potion, a damage-over-time status on the player. Start it once with no position (the edges of the whole screen pulse green with rising bubbles) and stop it when it wears off. For a poisoned character or enemy use state.poison; for a poison hit use magic.poison.

effects.name: ui.purchase
effects.whenToUse: A purchase succeeds in a shop: an item, skin, booster or upgrade bought with coins or gems, an in-app purchase confirmed, a deal paid for. Play with { el } on the Buy button or the item bought. For a free reward being claimed use ui.burst; for coins collected in play use pickup.coin.

effects.name: ui.rays
effects.whenToUse: Light rays turning behind a reward on a popup: a prize, trophy or chest on a reward screen, a new character or item being shown off, a daily-reward card. Play with { el, layer: 'back' } on the icon so the rays sit behind it; stop when the popup closes. For a chest bursting open use reward.chest; for a soft glow behind a button use ui.glow.

effects.name: ui.sparkle
effects.whenToUse: A special offer, sale, bundle or premium item in a shop or menu: sparkles circle around its button or card. Play with { el, follow: true } and stop it when it is bought or closed. For marking an unseen item use ui.new; for a pulsing glow behind a call-to-action use ui.glow; for a sparkle on an object in the game world use state.sparkle.

effects.name: ui.speedlines
effects.whenToUse: Anime speed lines over the whole screen: a speed boost or nitro, falling fast, a dramatic dash, a warp jump, a rush or fever mode. Start it once with no position and stop it when the speed ends. For lines streaming behind one moving character or car use move.speed; for inward manga lines on a dramatic moment use ui.focuslines.

effects.name: ui.tapburst
effects.whenToUse: Each tap on the big clickable thing in an idle or clicker game (the cookie, the coin, the ore, the monster), so every click pays out with coins and stars spraying up. Cheap enough for many taps a second; play it with { event }. For a plain tap ripple use ui.tap; for one coin collected use pickup.coin.

effects.name: ui.tapme
effects.whenToUse: A tutorial shows where to tap: the first move, the button the player must press next, a spot on the board, an onboarding step. Play with { el } (or { at: [x, y] }) on the spot and stop it when the player taps. For a soft hint on a puzzle tile use puzzle.hint; for drawing the eye to a button without teaching use ui.glow.

effects.name: ui.transition
effects.whenToUse: A screen or scene change: menu to level, one level to the next, opening the world map, a time skip. A bright sweep crosses the whole screen in about 0.75 s; swap the screen underneath as it passes the middle (about 0.25 s). Play it without a position; dir sets the way it travels (degrees, default 0 = left to right, 90 = upward). For a plain white flash use ui.flash.

effects.name: ui.victory
effects.whenToUse: A short victory screen moment: the win or results screen appears, a match or battle is won, a boss is beaten. Play it once with no position: golden rays shine from the middle of the screen while confetti falls over all of it (1.5 s). For a longer level-clear party with fireworks use reward.clear; for a confetti cannon fired from one spot use reward.confetti; for rays turning behind one prize on a popup use ui.rays.

effects.name: ui.wrongtry
effects.whenToUse: A gentle, friendly "not quite, try again" for young children: a wrong pick in a kids learning, toddler, spelling or counting game, where a red X would feel harsh. Play it with { el } on the chosen answer; the ring fits its size. For a clear wrong answer or invalid move use puzzle.wrong; for a right answer use ui.correct.
